legend: After a long night of pilfering the neighborhood of all the candy, Magikarp's friend group must call it day and go back home.

The neighborhood has $$$n$$$ homes numbered $$$1$$$ through $$$n$$$, connected by $$$m$$$ bidirectional streets. Each street takes one minute to walk along, and every home is reachable from every other home.
There are $$$k$$$ people in the group, including Magikarp. They are all currently at home $$$1$$$, and the $$$i$$$th person lives at home $$$a_i$$$. Several people may live at the same home.
They want to walk together for as long as possible, but nobody is willing to take a detour. This means that everyone must take some shortest path from home $$$1$$$ to their home.
What is the maximum number of streets the group can walk along together before splitting apart? They may split up immediately, in which case the answer is $$$0$$$.
input: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$k$$$ ($$$1\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0\le m\le \min(6\cdot 10^5,\frac{n(n-1)}{2})$$$, $$$1\le k\le 8000$$$) — the number of homes, the number of streets, and the number of people, respectively.
The second line contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$ ($$$1\le a_i\le n$$$) — the home of each person.
Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1\le u,v\le n$$$, $$$u\ne v$$$), describing a bidirectional street connecting homes $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$.
There is at most one street between any pair of homes. It is guaranteed that every home is reachable from home $$$1$$$.
output: Output a single integer — the maximum number of streets the group can walk along together.
note: In the first example, the group can walk from home $$$1$$$ to home $$$2$$$ and then to home $$$3$$$. The people living at homes $$$4$$$ and $$$5$$$ can then take their respective streets home. Both complete walks are shortest paths, so the answer is $$$2$$$.

In the second example, everyone can first walk to home $$$3$$$. One person then walks to home $$$4$$$, and the other walks to home $$$5$$$. Although there are two shortest paths to home $$$4$$$, they only need to choose one that allows the group to stay together.
In the third example, someone already lives at home $$$1$$$. They cannot walk along any street without taking a detour, so the group must split up immediately.

legend.ai: 在漫长的一夜洗劫了附近所有糖果后，鲤鱼王的朋友们只好收工回家。
该社区有 $$$n$$$ 栋房屋，编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$，由 $$$m$$$ 条双向街道连接。沿每条街道步行需要一分钟，并且每栋房屋都可以从其他任意房屋到达。
这个小组中共有 $$$k$$$ 个人，其中包括 Magikarp。他们目前都在家 $$$1$$$，第 $$$i$$$ 个人住在家 $$$a_i$$$。多个人可能住在同一个家中。
他们想要尽可能长时间地一起行走，但没有人愿意绕路。这意味着每个人都必须从家 $$$1$$$ 走某条最短路径回到自己的家。
这群人在分开之前最多可以一起走过多少条街道？他们可以立即分开，此时答案为 $$$0$$$。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 $$$n$$$、$$$m$$$ 和 $$$k$$$($$$1\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$、$$$0\le m\le \min(6\cdot 10^5,\frac{n(n-1)}{2})$$$、$$$1\le k\le 8000$$$)——分别表示房屋数量、街道数量和人数。
第二行包含 $$$k$$$ 个整数 $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$($$$1\le a_i\le n$$$)，表示每个人的家。
接下来的 $$$m$$$ 行中的每一行包含两个整数 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$($$$1\le u,v\le n$$$、$$$u\ne v$$$)，表示一条连接房屋 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$ 的双向街道。
任意一对房屋之间至多有一条街道。保证每个房屋都可以从房屋 $$$1$$$ 到达。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——小组可以一起步行经过的街道数量的最大值。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，这群人可以从房屋 $$$1$$$ 走到房屋 $$$2$$$，然后再走到房屋 $$$3$$$。居住在房屋 $$$4$$$ 和 $$$5$$$ 的人随后可以分别沿各自的街道回家。两条完整的行走路线都是最短路径，因此答案是 $$$2$$$。
在第二个样例中，所有人可以先一起走到家 $$$3$$$。随后，其中一个人走到家 $$$4$$$，另一个人走到家 $$$5$$$。尽管到家 $$$4$$$ 有两条最短路径，但他们只需选择其中一条能让队伍保持在一起的路径。
在第三个示例中，已经有人住在家 $$$1$$$。他们无法不绕道而沿任何一条街道行走，因此这群人必须立即分开。
